text:
The circularity of the AI capex problem

If you are worried about supply of fresh equity, why are those companies who benefit from the spend of this new capital being sold?

Why is everyone worried about dilution? Don't these projects have good margins with utility like demand than meta's business as a whole? There is a gap of a few years but tech investors have rarely been worried about things like that before.

The only proper sense bearish take to explain a day like today is that there will be insufficient demand for compute in the future and that all this spending is on a white elephant. I haven't really heard many make this case.

But I think it's the only thing that underlies these sort of moves. People doubt AI fundamentally and when they get asked to make a sacrifice for it (handing out capital), they flinch. It's not going to work, there's not enough demand. This makes selling across the AI supply chain rational.

Companies like coreweave are the ultimate expression of this. Individually unimportant in the whole scheme of things being opportunistic extremely highly leveraged (not just financially either, but to input pricing and execution risk) players that will just have their supply absorbed by someone else if they fail. There pricing offers a barometer in the belief in this future demand.

So, it's all just sentiment. And this makes sense. It's an enormous bet on something that is doubted by and is frightening to many and is many years into the future. Much harder than selling ads now.

AI has to generate enough economic productivity to pay for itself and the margins that justify these capital raises in the first place. I think it will. I don't think most agree and they are just getting pulled along as beta.

Even if it is successful in generating enough productivity to pay for itself (plus some juicy inference margin) you have many that are frightened of it in addition to doubting it. The corporate factory line worker is at risk just like they were to machines in the industrial revolution. This will prompt a response from government. How do you price that? By discounting the ROI on these investments?

This would get you to the point of being worried about dilution. The trade is just too uncertain and needs so much capital that the only realistic way it fails in the medium term is that we become forever compute constrained and AI has a small percentage of the effect it could've had, taking down the labs with it.

The New Humanity

A Dialogue from the Global Council

ELITIST: You still believe we want people to love one another?

CITIZEN: Isn’t that what you tell us? Unity. Diversity. A world without borders.

ELITIST: Unity is a useful slogan. What we actually want is uniformity. People who eat the same food, watch the same programs, speak the same approved language, and have forgotten why their grandparents ever fought to preserve anything.

CITIZEN: You want us to abandon our cultures?

ELITIST: Abandon? No. We want you to turn them into merchandise. Sell the costumes. Celebrate the festivals. Put the old traditions on television between advertisements. Keep the decorations; discard the convictions.

CITIZEN: And mixing every culture together will somehow make us easier to govern?

ELITIST: A population without a common memory is a population without a common purpose. Give people a thousand identities, a million distractions, and a thousand reasons to distrust their neighbors. Then offer them one authority capable of managing the chaos.

CITIZEN: So you manufacture the problem and sell yourselves as the solution.

ELITIST: Now you’re learning.

CITIZEN: And what happens to the people who refuse?

ELITIST: They become inconvenient. We call them backward, intolerant, or dangerous. We don’t need to silence every dissenter. We merely need to make dissent socially expensive.

CITIZEN: And the ruling class? Will your children live under the same system?

ELITIST: Of course not. Our children will attend the finest schools, live behind secure gates, and inherit the institutions that manage everyone else’s lives.

CITIZEN: Then this isn’t equality. It’s an aristocracy wearing the mask of progress.

ELITIST: Every age has its aristocracy. The clever ones simply learn to call theirs something more appealing.

CITIZEN: And what do you call yours?

ELITIST: Global governance. Sustainable development. Human cooperation. Choose whichever phrase makes you sleep best.

CITIZEN: One world, ruled by a few.

ELITIST: Precisely. And the beautiful part is that the public will argue endlessly about the slogans while we consolidate the power.

CITIZEN: You think people are too stupid to see what you’re doing.

ELITIST: No. I think people are too busy, too divided, and too exhausted to do anything about it.

CITIZEN: And if they finally wake up?

ELITIST: Then we will tell them that the world is too complicated to run without us.

The Citizen looks through the glass wall at the city below: a thousand flags in the museums, a thousand languages fading from the streets, and one enormous emblem glowing above the government tower.

CITIZEN: You haven’t united humanity.

ELITIST: What have we done, then?

CITIZEN: You’ve made the whole world a kingdom—and convinced the people they elected the king.

For the first time, the Elitist says nothing.

Kent, the bible doesn't say that Cain "brought the fruit of the ground" .  The KJV says "brought of the fruit of the ground". Cain’s Offering: Fruit on the Ground

Genesis 4:3 describes Cain’s offering with an unusual phrase: **מִפְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה** (*mipperî hāʾădāmāh*)—“from the fruit of the ground.” My argument is that this wording may describe fruit associated with the ground itself—fruit already lying on Cain’s ground. Cain's ground fits the Hebrew well.
1. The wording is distinctive
The Bible refers to fruit many times. Before that verse, depending on the translation Fruit is mentioned up to 9 time but Genesis 4:3 uses a notably different construction: “fruit of the ground.” That difference deserves interpretive weight. If the author meant ordinary cultivated produce, why describe Cain’s gift this way rather than with the more familiar language used everywhere for fruit in the bible and elsewhere?
The Hebrew phrase unusual wording, used no where else, invites us to ask, is that the reason Cain's offering had no respect?

2. The earlier uses of “fruit” provide a frame of reference
The earlier biblical references to fruit establish a pattern for what “fruit” means and how it is described. Genesis 4:3 should be read in light of that foundation, not as though *perî* automatically means any agricultural produce. The contrast between those earlier descriptions and Cain’s wording may signal that something about his offering was unusual.

3. The offerings are contrasted, and Cain’s is rejected
Abel brings the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions. Cain’s gift is described differently, and the Lord has no respect for it. The passage does not explicitly explain the reason for the rejection, but the contrast makes the nature and quality of Cain’s offering relevant. If his gift consisted of fruit already "sacrificed to" the ground.

4. Fallen fruit is sacrificed by the tree.
If the fruit had fallen from the tree, it could be understood as something the tree had already given up. Cain would then be presenting something already sacrifice by its source, rather than offering a fresh gift of his own. On this reading, it would not function as a genuine sacrifice: something already given up cannot be sacrificed a second time would have no respect from the Lord.

5. The Lord came down and warned Cain. 
The Lord didn't even mention the fruit. The Lord's only concern was how angry Cain was at Abel, that tells us he murdered his brother for an underlying reason, not the Lord's lack of respect.

6. Nowhere in the Bible does fruit come from anywhere except a tree, a womb, a vine, a limb, or a market. 

Conclusion   
Taken together—the one and only use of that Hebrew wording, the earlier biblical pattern for “fruit,” the contrast between Cain’s and Abel’s offerings, Hermeneutics, and Cain’s rejection—these details support that Cain brought fruit already lying on his ground, rather than a fresh, deliberately offered harvest aka a sacrifice. 
This is the only coherent explanation for why Cain’s offering was described differently and was not accepted and the Lord did not mention the fruit to Cain.

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

A degree earned years ago is not a license, and a man who ran a city health department from an office is not the practicing physician voters picture when they hear the title. Letting voters picture someone else is not a rounding error. It is the campaign.
Mike Rogers offers Michigan a record voters can check. El-Sayed offers a biography that dissolves the moment anyone checks it, and a debate performance that started with the claim his own licensing record refutes. If a candidate will stretch the truth about himself in the first five seconds, voters should ask what he will stretch in the United States Senate.

October 22, 2026 | Colorado Front Range

Emergency crews, law enforcement officers, animal control personnel and transportation officials responded to numerous incidents across the Colorado Front Range Thursday afternoon and evening. text:
The same day Michael Rosenblum disappeared, police found the car he was driving and towed it to their lot.

His family didn't find out for three months.

It was Valentine's Day 1980, near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Michael was 25 and fighting an addiction to prescription painkillers. The night before, a month after rehab, his mother found pills in his room and told him to leave until he was clean. She later said she would blame herself until the day she died.

The next morning, he dropped his girlfriend off at a gas station and drove off in her car. He said he would meet her at his parents' house in two hours. He never arrived. His money stayed in the bank and his clothes stayed in his closet.

Pittsburgh police searched for the car for two weeks. His father, Maurice, put up flyers, offered a reward and traveled as far as California. Over the years he spent nearly a quarter of a million dollars looking for his son.

That May, police in the suburb of Baldwin Borough told the girlfriend they had her car. An officer had found it on River Road two hours after Michael left her, with two flat tires, no keys and a cold engine. Police said they had mailed her a letter the next day. She said it never came.

Then it got stranger. An anonymous caller told Maurice his son had been arrested by Baldwin police. That July, Baldwin police issued a warrant for Michael over a burglary committed two months after he vanished. The victims had described a man in mirrored sunglasses, but the sketch showed his whole face. The warrant was dropped a week later.

Years later, the police chief's secretary said that months after the tow, the chief had him write a letter to the car's owner dated the day after the car was found. He said he filed it and never mailed it. In 1987 the borough council fired the chief for interfering with the investigation. A civil service commission reinstated him, finding no misconduct, and a state investigation had found no evidence of wrongdoing.

In 1992, a hiker found part of a human skull in the woods near River Road. Tests confirmed it was Michael's. After 12 years, his parents could finally bury their son. How and why he died has never been determined, and no one has ever been charged.

His parents got their son back, but never the answer they spent 12 years looking for.

What do you think happened to Michael that day?

The Collectivist Delusion: Why Aristotle and Marx Fail the Test of Biblical Truth

In the theater of political philosophy, modern leftists often attempt to cloak their radical economic engineering in the respectable robes of antiquity. They point to Karl Marx’s deep admiration for Aristotle—specifically the ancient Greek assertion that man is merely a politikon zoon, a "political animal"—as proof that human beings are meant to be subjugated to a collective whole.
But this intellectual lineage reveals a deeper, more troubling truth: both Aristotelian paganism and Marxist socialism share a fundamental flaw. They subordinate the sacred, God-given sovereignty of the individual to the tyranny of the collective, whether that collective is called the polis or the proletariat. This pagan-materialist synthesis stands in direct opposition to the true, foundational principles of Western civilization rooted in the Holy Scriptures.

The Pagan State as an Idol

When Aristotle claimed in his Politics that the state is logically "prior to the individual" and that those living outside it are "either beasts or gods," he laid the groundwork for state worship. In the pagan worldview, a man’s worth was derived entirely from his utility to the city-state.
Marxism merely modernized this pagan idolatry. By replacing the Greek polis with the socialist collective and redefining man as a "species-being" (Gattungswesen), Marx stripped humanity of individual soul and free will. In both systems, the individual is reduced to an interchangeable cog in a grand political machine. Whether forced to serve an ancient aristocratic elite or a modern bureaucratic dictatorship of the proletariat, the results are identical: the erasure of personal autonomy and the destruction of true freedom.

The Biblical Contrast: Sovereign Individuals under God

The Holy Scriptures offer a radically different, far more elevated understanding of the human condition—one that completely rejects the collectivism of both the Greek marketplace and the Marxist manifesto.
Created in the Image of God (Imago Dei): Genesis 1:27 establishes that God created man in His own image—as individuals, not as a faceless collective. Human dignity does not depend on a relationship to a state (polis) or an economic class, but on a direct, personal relationship with the Creator.
Individual Free Will and Moral Responsibility: The Bible places the burden of moral choice squarely on the individual. In Ezekiel 18:20, Scripture declares that "the soul who sins is the one who will die" and that a son will not bear the iniquity of the father. Salvation and damnation are individual matters, completely incompatible with Marxist notions of collective class guilt or Aristotle's civic determinism.
The Sanctity of Private Property and Family: While Marx demanded the total abolition of private property and the traditional family, and Aristotle sought state regulation of the household, the Bible firmly protects both. The Commandments "Thou shalt not steal" and "Thou shalt not covet" inherently legitimize private ownership. Property and inheritance are viewed as fruits of honest labor and blessings from God to be managed by families, not tools of production to be seized and redistributed by a predatory state.

True Charity vs. Compulsory Solidarity

Apologists for socialism often try to conflate the early Christian voluntary sharing of goods (as seen in the Book of Acts) with Marxist state coercion. This is a profound misreading of Scripture. Biblical charity is rooted in voluntary, individual giving born of a transformed heart (2 Corinthians 9:7: "Each man should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not reluctantly or under compulsion").
In contrast, Marxist socialism relies on the raw power of the state to confiscate property, stoke class envy, and enforce a gray, uniform equality. Where the Bible preaches love, personal responsibility, and spiritual redemption, Marxism and pagan collectivism offer only materialist envy, state worship, and the crushing of the individual spirit.

Reclaiming the Foundation

The historical link between Aristotle's politikon zoon and Marxist socialism serves as a stark warning. When a society divorces itself from the transcendent truths of the Bible, it invariably slides back into pagan collectivism, elevating the government or the collective into the position of God.
True freedom, economic prosperity, and moral order cannot be found by looking to the pagan city-states of the past or the failed socialist experiments of the modern era. They are preserved only when we recognize that man is not a political animal bound to the state, but a sovereign creation accountable to God alone.

I'd like to share a little about what I've been working on at my new company @ultrametricai with my cofounder @tylerlastovich. We have been exploring how we could automate the startup itself, leaving founders with more time to focus on their exact mission.

Enter our first release of the Open Startup Repo: https://t.co/ecZZRU9iX4

A common foundation for transparent automation of the startup. 

After close to 20 years in silicon valley, backing hundreds of amazing founders & startups, being in the trenches of founding Heyzap (YC08), then solo founding @golden, going through 2 acquisitions and working behind the scenes with some of the iconic companies today, I'm witnessing the largest change to how we work I could have imagined - a truly monumental era of creative abundance. 

I believe the next generation of companies will largely run themselves: from operations, code, product upgrades, growth, vendor control & selection, process execution, special situations, strategy etc etc. That leaves founder time for 'the art' at the very niche core: the (currently) unautomatable, the special leaps humans tend to make, and north star setting.

We want founders to go super deep into the main problem they are trying to solve and not get held up doing anything else, from searching for domain availability with trademark checks to setting their company up, to running their processes on autopilot. 

So to help that broad foundational layer for starting and running a company, we have spent around a year exploring how to help founders focus on their mission across different verticals, geos, stages and initial starting conditions.

Our first few attempts at making something useful actually failed as the market and AI was moving so fast; it just got absorbed into the models or other product releases. We saw polsia happen, openclaw, then grokbot, muse, dots, etc era as the astras, fables, opuses, kimis and jevs rolled out. What seemed to have been missing along the way was a common repo to identify, unify, open and normalize all the lego bricks that startups have to interact with (vendors, processes, business logic, law, best practices, surface areas, art of the possible). 

As the number of software vendors blew up, the interfaces to drive them multiplied, the international startup founder blew up as silicon valley moved from a specific location to a state of mind and global movement. Unlimited pre seed funding in unlimited vertical sub markets and permutations has brought us to the age of infinity but we have yet to achieve being able to type into an agent a very simple sentence with very complex implications 'just setup my company and make $1m/m'. We have ended up with a hybrid mismash of computer use, API calls, plugins, shifting surface areas (API/MCP/CLI/plugins/chats/musish futures), and changing model absorption to vendor balance making it an exciting and unstable time. 

As our first step we started to rank all the vendors that startups interface to when going about their journey in terms of how agentically controllable they are via their APIs, MCPs, CLIs etc and computer use compatibility as we are largely switching from a UI driven world to the agentic control surfaces and onto full automation. We have 100 ranking areas you can check out with an overall open ranking here: https://t.co/V6XRMME0Ib

Then we looked at the processes that startups do and how the vendors rank for the sub steps or process as a whole and how this changes across geos. Open processes: https://t.co/iSQ90poYxq

Then we started to hack on an open repo for startups that would contain all the components we are going to need for a common foundation for founders across the globe even if our gov processes vary so much from Bengaluru to SF or Lisbon to Shenzhen.  The founder spirit is geo-invariant. 

We have looked at special founder/startup situations, the business logic that will make open modules for the startup that we can hack on together, ranked law firms, government services and interfaces, stacks that go well together. We have mapped the law and lore that maps to startups and the schemas that make up the data objects and documents. But also the open documents and the missing gaps. MUCH TO DO.

All the BS processes and fluff work that founders waste their time on needs to goto zero. I want to see more supersonic planes, cancer drugs, seemingly impossible missions done and increase the bang for buck founders have with their funding. 

This is a work in progress and we are keen for the community to come hack on the repo with us here: https://t.co/ecZZRU9iX4

Lets get into the structure of the general repo and the visualizations we made on https://t.co/XEYK9ipnfI site with example links:

- Open law (we are interested in how law changes the processes, situations and normalizing this over time) https://t.co/5yJnYbC0bk

- Open lore (we are interested in the historical lore of startups, the rules of thumb and heuristics that might guide your agent): https://t.co/gjliXoQwe1

- Open fields (we are interested in how the schema for the data connects to the open modules, business logic, open documents and artifacts of each process eg how is a EIN defined?) https://t.co/59rcEXhnCx

- Open documentation (eg SAFE notes and missing! docs) https://t.co/BbvBow2Olt

We have looked at YC companies as well in terms of which ones do well agentically: https://t.co/snnJ83r9ly

We are interested in stacks and how people are changing their work: https://t.co/wFHoew5V9I

We are interested in what is automatable and where the agentic ceiling is currently and how to push that up in all areas: https://t.co/WmTDjmNyV4

There is more for you to explore and a lot more coming in terms of how you will be able to navigate business in an optimal way in your chosen surface area; whether you are hanging in grokbot, dots, muse, claude, terminal, chat, or whatever is coming up in this exciting time. 

We have a lot of data to collect, clean up and help agents navigate the vast landscape emerging functionality the entire startup ecosystem has to offer. 

Come join us getting your vendor in, ranked or that access pattern you have wanted or getting the data more accurate in terms of which vendor is best for a process or steps. Or open a module of something that currently cost money that could be free. 

Also come play in our discord for founders and join the chaos (we can solve each others issues including fund raising tips from me personally): https://t.co/AmBtzFy0Bz 

It's time to lift all the boats in the harbor and I'm extremely excited as to what the community of hackers and painters will hack into the repo, what asks they will have and whether we can shift normalization of processes globally, gov agentic interfaces and have common repo for founders that grows over time. I expect a lot of experimentation along the way, bugs and upside...

PPS: we have other stuff to launch we just thought this was a great place to start and have 200 PRs coming out pretty soon but I still want to know what is broken or doesnt make sense or inaccurate.

Ricci Road in Dayton, Nevada, is named after the historic Ricci family and the Ricci Ranch, a prominent Italian-American family that pioneered local agriculture and ranching along the Carson River. 

Key Details
Family Roots: Bernardo Ricci moved to Dayton from Lucca, Italy, around 1900, and built the family ranch house on the property in 1912.

Location & Infrastructure: Ricci Road marks the eastern terminus of Nevada State Route 822 (which starts at US Route 50 and crosses the Carson River over the historic 1956 bridge).

“As the chairman of this committee, speaking for my associates,
with their consent, and with the approval of General
Washington, I respectfully invite the Professor to meet with the
Committee as one of its members; and we, each one, personally
and urgently, request h im to accept the responsibility, and to give
us, and the American Colonies, the benefit of his counsel.”
Taking the floor, the Professor accepted the responsibility.
Then, startlingly, he proposed that his disciple, the hostess, be
placed on the committee “because she is our hostess, because she
is a woman, and above all, because she is a superior woman.” (The
committee considered this an innovation; yet the Jesuits had been
employing female coadjutors for centuries.) The proposal was “immediately
and unanimously adopted.” Luncheon was adjourned.
The committee would reconvene at seven in the evening, “in the
guest chamber usually occupied by the Professor.”
Franklin and the Professor spent the afternoon together walking
about Cambridge. When they returned, the hostess noted that
“both of them wore the relieved and confident look of earnest and
determined men who had, in a satisfactory way, solved a perplexRULERS
OF EVIL
ing problem, and of victors who had successfully mastered a difficult
and dangerous situation.”
At the evening session, Franklin turned the meeting over to
“his new-found and abundantly honored friend.” The subject was
a flag. Addressing the committee as “Comrade Americans,” the
Professor explained that, since the colonies were still dependent
upon Great Britain, “we are not expected to design or recommend
a flag which will represent a new government or an independent
nation,” but instead one “that will testify our present loyalty as
English Subjects,” a flag that was “already in use,” a flag that had
been recognized by the British government for “half a century,” a
flag having a field of alternate horizontal red and white stripes with
the Grand Union Flag of Great Britain in the upper left corner.
“I refer,” he said, “to the flag of the East India Company.”
To hide the fact that Americans would be fighting under the
private flag of an international mercantile corporation controlled
by Jesuits, the Professor provided a plausible cover whereby the flag
could be “explained to the masses:”
“The Union Flag of the Mother Country is retained as the
union [upper left corner] of our new flag to announce that the
Colonies are loyal to the just and legitimate sovereignty of the
British Government. The thirteen stripes will at once be understood
to represent the thirteen Colonies; their equal width will
type the equal rank, rights and responsibilities of the Colonies.
The union of the stripes in the field of our flag will announce the
unity of interests and the cooperative union of efforts, which the
Colonies recognize and put forth in their common cause. The
white stripes will signify that we consider our demands just and
reasonable; and that we will seek to secure our rights through
peaceable, intelligent and statesmanlike means – if they prove
at all possible; and the red stripes at the top and bottom of our
flag will declare that first and last – and always – we have the
determination, the enthusiasm, and the power to use force –
whenever we deem force necessary. The alternation of the red
and white stripes will suggest that our reasons for all demands
will be intelligent and forcible, and that our force in securing our
rights will be just and reasonable.”

The Professor reminded the committee that “the masses of the
people, and a large majority of the leaders of public opinion, desire
a removal of grievances, and a rectification of wrongs, through a
fuller recognition of their rights as British Subjects; and few of
them desire and very few of them expect – at this time – any complete
severance of their present political and dependent relations
with the English Government.” That severance would occur
“before the sun in its next summer’s strength” – indicating that the
Professor foreknew, as Lorenzo Ricci would have foreknown, a July
declaration of independence. At that time, the East India Company
flag could be “easily modified” by replacing the Union Jack with
stars against a blue background, “to make it announce and represent
the new and independent nation.”
Washington and Franklin lavished the Professor’s idea with
“especial approval and unstinted praise.” The committee formally
and unanimously adopted the East India Company’s banner,
known as “The Thirteen Stripes,” as the “general flag and recognized
standard of the Colonial Army and Navy.” Just before midnight,
they adjourned.
On January 2, 1776, at a formal ceremony attended by the Flag
Committee, George Washington personally hoisted the East India
Company flag “upon a towering and specially raised pine tree liberty
pole,” unfurling it to the breeze and displaying it for the first
time “to his army, the citizens of the vicinity, and the British forces
in Boston.” The British officers at Charlestown Heights perceived
the event
to mean that General Washington had thus announced his surrender
to them. At once, they saluted “The Thirteen Stripes”
with thirteen hearty cheers. They immediately followed this
spontaneous outburst of British Enthusiasm with the grander
and more dignified official salute of thirteen guns, the thirteengun
salute being the highest compliment in gunpowder, the military
“God speed you.”
By so colorfully equivocating both his enemies, the Professor
had made himself G o d of Confusion. The redcoats were toasting
RULERS OF EVIL
the good health of the rebels, who in turn were fighting for the
East India Company. One of the few places in the world where
such ludicrous phenomena are considered standard and routine is
in the pages of Lorenzo Ricci’s Thirteen Articles: “The General
decides everything; he knows how to shape, at will, not only the
army he is commanding but also that of his enemies.”
LORENZO Ricci’s post-mortem attendance in America is strongly
suggested in yet another pivotal episode, the famous “mission
to Canada.” This strange exercise is normally regarded by
historians as a colossal failure. It began on February 15, 1776,
when the Second Continental Congress resolved to send Benjamin
Franklin, Samuel Chase, and Charles Carroll to Montreal
with full authority “to promote or form a union” with Canada
against England.
Just before the committee left Philadelphia, John Adams proposed
a curious last-minute resolution. On the record, he requested
“that Charles Carroll prevail on Mr. John Carroll to accompany
the committee to Canada, to assist them in such matters as they shall
think useful.” Congress adopted the resolution.
How might a priest have assisted the committee in promoting
or forming a union with Canada? T h e answer lies in demographics.
Canada then was largely Quebec, and Quebec, though ruled
despotically by the British since 1763, was mostly Roman
Catholic. A Jesuit priest, armed with the right Vatican paperwork
or password, could exert powerful influence on Canadian foreign
policy. The same priest, if accompanied by the combined head of
the black papacy and international Freemasonry, could make that
policy.
The mission arrived in Montreal only to learn that Bishop
Briand of Quebec had ordered Pierre Floquet, the Jesuit superior
in Montreal, to consider John Carroll persona non grata. Floquet,
however, defied his bishop and invited Carroll to say a mass in his
home anyway, for which Floquet was immediately suspended from
his priestly functions. The incident colored the mission with disaster
(although Floquet was restored, according to Walsh’s Ameri-can Jesuits, after a simple apology). Disaster was verified when the
committee returned to Philadelphia with no prospect for any
union whatsoever with Canada. Congress lamented that America’s
first diplomatic legation had failed.
But America’s first diplomatic legation was Sun-Tzuan and
Jesuitic, and Jesuit diplomacy can be expected to conceal victory
behind mishap. As the Thirteen Articles put it, “You must have a
real advantage when the enemy believes you have sustained some
losses.” So we examine the Canadian mishap for a real advantage
and discover something far more valuable than the originallysought
union. While Bishop Briand was outwardly demeaning
John Carroll, the mission was obtaining from Canada a position of
neutrality. This was a significant achievement, considering Canada’s
good relationship with Great Britain on the one hand and two
centuries of hostilities toward New England on the other. For the
colonists, Canadian neutrality removed the threat of a powerful
northwestern enemy and cleared the way for a declaration of independence.
At Montreal, as at Cambridge, I sense the presence of
someone infinitely more commanding than mere committeemen
appointed by Congress. I sense the presence of the “honorary”
committeeman unlisted in any record – the Professor, the fugitive
Vicar of Christ.
Returning from Canada, Benjamin Franklin fell ill. It was John
Carroll who escorted him to Philadelphia. At Franklin’s invitation,
Carroll moved into his home. Franklin acknowledged the
fact in a letter dated May 27, 1776, mentioning “Mr. Carroll’s
friendly assistance and tender care of me.” These were critical
weeks of countdown to the Declaration of Independence. I wonder
who else might have been found under the Franklin roof? Perhaps
the Professor, with his dynamic oaken chest?
Philadelphia was crawling just now with social activists from
all over, the very people Lorenzo Ricci had appointed John Carroll,
as Prefect of the Sodality, to organize. The home of America’s
pre-eminent Freemason, with Carroll and perhaps even Ricci in
residence, would have become the main clearing-house for sub
rosa congressional business.
RULERS OF EVIL
ON July 3, 1776, John Adams took pen in hand and dashed off
a letter to his wife Abigail. Adams was a writer of Mozartean
facility, concentration, and confidence. Everything he ever wrote
was first-draft and good. He never struck through words, never
edited. His moving hand, having writ, just moved on. “Yesterday,”
he scribbled,
the greatest question was decided which ever was debated in
America, and a greater, perhaps, never was nor will be decided
among men. A resolution was passed without one dissenting
colony, that these United Colonies are, and of right ought to
have, full power to make war, conclude peace, establish commerce,
and to do all other acts and things which other States
may rightfully do. The second day of July 1776 will be the most
memorable date in the history of America. I am apt to believe
that it will be celebrated by succeeding generations as the great
anniversary festival. It ought to be commemorated as the day of
deliverance, by solemn acts of devotion to God Almighty. It
ought to be solemnized with pomp and parade, with shows,
games, sports, guns, bells, bonfires, and illuminations, from one
end of this continent to the other, from this time forward,
forevermore.
If the black papacy truly had orchestrated America’s breakaway
from England, we would expect to find the second day of July to be
rich in cabalah and in Roman Catholic liturgical color. The Liturgical
Calendar is a process, authorized nowhere in the Bible,
through which faithful Catholics may plead with Almighty God
for favors through the merits of ascended saints on special feast
days. Supposedly, the prayerful performance of an act on a date the
Church has consecrated to a saint endows the act with the mystique
of the saint as well as the saint’s intercessory prayers to God
for success.
Maryland history, for example, is grounded in the Liturgical
Calendar. We recall how the original settlers of Maryland, many
of whom were Roman Catholics, set sail from England, under the
spiritual direction of Jesuit father Andrew White, on November
22, 1633. November 22 is the Feast Day of St. Cecilia, a third cen-tury Roman martyr and traditional patroness of musicians. Did
Cecilia’s spirit bless the voyage with musicality to cheer up an otherwise
oppressive boredom? T h e voyagers reached landfall the following
year on March 25, Annunciation Day, feast of the angel
Gabriel’s announcement to the Virgin Mary that she is pregnant
with the Son of God. Annunciation Day contains the joyful mystery
of an angel’s announcing the planting of the divine seed within
a virgin matrix. Did the settlers imagine themselves planting
the seed of a new social order in a strange wilderness, the whole
enterprise blessed by God through the merits of the Virgin Mary’s
unique relationship to Him? Then, exactly one year later, on
Annunciation Day 1634, Father White consecrated the colony of
Maryland to the Virgin Mary.
The second day of July in the year 1776 was Visitation Day,
commemorating the event recorded in the first chapter of Luke
wherein the Virgin, pregnant with the Messiah, visits her cousin
Elizabeth, who is pregnant with John the Baptist. (Nowadays Visitation
Day is celebrated on May 31, but in the year 1776 it was celebrated
on July second, as it had been celebrated, according to the
New Catholic Encyclopedia’s article entitled “Visitation of Mary,”
every year since the Council of Basel in 1441.)
No day in the Liturgical Calendar is more suited to Bellarminian
liberation theology than Visitation Day. Ste. Margaret-Marie
Alacoque, whose visions inspired the Jesuit social-action cult of
Sacred Heart, was a member of the Visitandines, an order of nuns
devoted to the Visitation. Visitation Day’s scriptural basis is the
Virgin Mary’s ecstatic sermon to Elizabeth at Luke 1:46-55. This
famous ejaculation, known as the Magnificat (the opening word
in the Latin Vulgate’s rendering of the passage, meaning “it magnifies”),
literally defines the social action called for by Sacred Heart
in Philadelphia on the second day of July, 1776:
My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced
in God my Saviour. For he hath regarded the low estate of his
handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall
call me blessed. For he that is mighty hath done to me great
things; and holy is his name. And his mercy is on them that fear

h im from generation to generation. He hath shewed strength
with his arm; he hath scattered the proud in the imagination of
their hearts. He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and
exalted them of low degree. He hath filled the hungry with good
things; and the rich he hath sent empty away....
Scattered the proud, put down the mighty, exalted them of low
degree, filled the hungry, emptied the rich.... This is the rhetoric of
Christian redemption, yes, but in the context of Lorenzo Ricci’s
agenda it’s the rhetoric of rebellion-to-tyranny, the very point of
the Declaration of Independence, and it’s spoken by the Virgin
Mary, Patroness of the Society of Jesus, Patroness of Maryland,

Saint Martin of Tours my patron Saint 

Saint Martin of Tours (c. 316–397) was a Roman soldier who became a monk and then Bishop of Tours. He is one of the most widely venerated early Western saints and a clear model of conversion that begins inside military life and continues into disciplined service of Christ.

He was born in Sabaria in Pannonia (modern Hungary) to pagan parents; his father was a military tribune. As a youth he was drawn to Christianity and became a catechumen against his family’s wishes. At about fifteen he was required by law to enter the Roman army and served as a cavalryman. While stationed at Amiens, still unbaptized, he met a half-naked beggar in the cold. He cut his military cloak in two with his sword and gave half to the man. That night he saw Christ wearing the half-cloak and heard the words that Martin the catechumen had clothed him. He was baptized shortly afterward.
Later, when offered a war bounty, he refused further combat service, declaring that he was now a soldier of Christ and it was not lawful for him to fight. He was discharged, placed himself under St. Hilary of Poitiers, lived as a hermit and monk, and founded the monastic community at Ligugé—one of the earliest in Gaul. In 371 or 372 he was made Bishop of Tours, largely against his will. He spent the rest of his life preaching, destroying pagan shrines, caring for the poor, and living simply. He died in 397 at Candes. His early life was written by his disciple Sulpicius Severus; the Catholic Encyclopedia summarizes the same sequence. Feast day: 11 November (memorial). He is patron of soldiers, the poor and defenseless. 

How he’s my patron Saint 
Retired army veteran recovering from major surgery, dealing with depression and trying to build daily structure through Scripture, prayer, and small practical steps. Martin’s path matches the stage you are in more closely than most soldier-saints.

Military service came first. Being faithful happened while he was still under military obligation, not after a complete break. My faith formation is also happening after active duty has ended but while im still working out the discipline of life after 26 years of service to my country as Saint Martin did to Rome 

He deliberately left the army for a life of prayer and ordered service rather than remaining in the old pattern. 

The cloak act was small, limited, and practical—he gave half of what he had on him. Current capacity is also limited by recovery; ordered care (pets, short walks, consistent short prayer, study and caring for others) fits the same scale.

As bishop he accepted responsibility he did not seek and kept living simply while doing the work. That combination of duty and humility fits a you who is trying to stay faithful without dramatic external activity.

Having him as a patron means asking his intercession for the specific transition I’m living: from soldier to disciple, from low drive to steady small acts, and from recovery into a structured life of faith. The Church permits personal choice of a patron; Martin’s documented life supplies usable examples rather than only a single dramatic moment.

EARTH: THE NEXUS OF THE GRIMM UNIVERSE

Earth deserves its own place beside Myst, Wonderland, Neverland and Oz. It is easy to treat it as the familiar world we leave when the real adventure begins, but that misses a lot of what Grimm Fairy Tales is doing. The other realms have their own conflicts. Earth is where those conflicts can turn up in somebody's home, school, workplace or city, and where people have to figure out what they are actually dealing with.

The basic arrangement is four main realms connected through Earth, the Nexus. That is why I am covering five settings in this series even though the phrase Four Realms keeps coming up. The count changes because Earth is being included in the discussion, not because Myst has disappeared or another name has been swapped in.

Being the Nexus makes Earth important to the larger setting, but I would not turn that word into an explanation for every supernatural event. It does not mean every person on Earth knows the realms exist. It does not mean every visitor has the same abilities here. It gives us the relationship between the worlds, and then the individual stories show what that relationship means for the people caught in it.

The original Grimm Fairy Tales begins on a much more personal scale than an army crossing dimensions. Sela Mathers brings fairy tales into the lives of people facing bad choices, with supernatural visions that make those stories immediate and dangerous. Belinda uses a similar ability for very different ends. Before we get the larger conflicts, there is already a question about who gets to use that influence and what they are trying to accomplish with it.

That early structure matters to Earth's identity. This is a setting where a familiar conversation can become an encounter with something the person does not understand. The danger does not have to begin with someone announcing that magic exists. It can begin with someone wanting something badly enough to ignore the consequences, or accepting an explanation that makes the wrong choice easier.

As the universe grows, Earth becomes a place where supernatural life is organized as well as hidden. The government is not simply absent from the picture. HiboCorp appears in the earlier Realm Knights material as an institution dealing with Highborns, and the Realm Knights bring powerful individuals into missions with official involvement. The existence of an organization does not make it trustworthy, and a mission briefing does not necessarily tell its participants everything they need to know.

That adds a different kind of pressure from the kingdoms of Myst or the rulers of Oz. On Earth, somebody can be treated as a person, an asset, a danger or a subject of investigation depending on who is looking at them. A supernatural origin does not protect anyone from bureaucracy, secrecy or manipulation. It may be exactly what attracts that attention.

The original Red Agent series brings this into a more modern action setting. Britney Waters works with Avril Williams and Ditto against the Circle. The story puts a witch and a Highborn hacker in the same operation, alongside an android and laboratory-enhanced danger. Those details are worth keeping separate. Technology has not vanished because magic exists, and having supernatural help does not remove the need for other skills.

The combination gives Earth a range the individual realm labels do not immediately suggest. A supernatural threat can be tied to research, surveillance or an organized group instead of a castle or an ancient throne. Someone can have access to extraordinary abilities and still need information, allies and a workable plan. The setting lets those things matter together.

Marian's presence on Earth is another useful example. Coming from Myst gives her a different relationship to the modern world. Pat Shand has discussed her fascination with human culture, and that perspective brings some ordinary life back into a universe full of danger. Earth is strange to her in ways it is not strange to someone who grew up here. Its music, habits and everyday experiences are part of the setting too.

There is a difference between being from Earth and living on Earth. That sounds obvious until every character in a city starts getting grouped together as if they have the same background. A witch from Myst, a person with a supernatural inheritance and an ordinary human encountering something impossible can all share a street without sharing a history. Their different starting points are part of what makes the world work.

Hellchild pushes that mixture into another corner. Angelica Blackstone is Hades' daughter and combines divine and vampiric elements. The original series places her story among characters including Van Helsing and Marian, with the supernatural conflict taking place in New York. That does not turn Earth into a separate vampire realm. It shows how a very specific supernatural history can become part of life here.

It also shows why a list of inhabitants is not enough to explain a world. Angelica's background matters to her story, but it does not define how every other person on Earth functions. The same goes for a witch, a Highborn or a monster hunter. They can cross paths without all becoming examples of one common power system.

At the beginning of Arcane Acre, the focus also includes young Highborns and the responsibility of helping them deal with their abilities. I am keeping that to the setup rather than running ahead through the school's later stories. The important shift is already there: what happens after you recognize that someone has power? Protecting the world includes deciding how to teach, guide and support people who have to live with it.

That question belongs naturally on Earth. It puts the supernatural beside the ordinary problem of growing up and learning how to make decisions. A powerful ability can change the scale of a mistake without making its owner more prepared to handle the situation. An institution can offer help, but it also raises questions about responsibility and trust.

Earth therefore has several overlapping layers. There is everyday life. There are people whose supernatural lives remain personal or concealed. There are organizations trying to control what they know. There are visitors carrying histories from other realms. There are larger conflicts that can force those layers together whether anyone is ready or not.

For these posts, I am treating those layers as the foundation rather than trying to squeeze every faction, creature and future event into one article. The detailed team breakdowns and creature guides have their own place. Earth needs room to be understood as a setting first.

The Nexus is where Grimm Fairy Tales can bring its fantasy back into a recognizable world and ask what people would actually do with it. Some want to help. Some want power. Some want to survive. Some are trying to build a life while all of those other motives collide around them. That is enough to make Earth a full part of the series, rather than just the place everyone starts before going somewhere more interesting.

I’m still putting together a guide to how magic works in this world. I’ll be posting that shortly.

How Magic Works in Wonderland

Wonderland's magic is easiest to understand when the different kinds of danger are kept separate. A portal can move someone between worlds. An artifact can give its holder a particular advantage. A powerful being can be imprisoned within a person's mind. The realm's influence can also persist after someone has physically escaped it.

Those effects belong to the same setting, but they do not automatically share one mechanism. Treating every strange event as unlimited reality manipulation makes the world harder to understand, especially when the characters have to find a particular weapon, reach a particular place, or stop a particular enemy.

This guide covers the early Wonderland material available around the beginning of Arcane Acre. It concentrates on crossings, corruption, dangerous objects, and individual supernatural abilities. Later explanations of the realm and a full breakdown of its creatures belong elsewhere.

Crossing between worlds

The looking glass is the most recognizable connection between Earth and Wonderland. It makes an ordinary object into a threshold, which is part of why the threat can enter spaces that should feel private. A mirror in this mythology can have a history and a supernatural purpose beyond its everyday appearance.

That does not establish that every mirror is a portal. The relevant objects and circumstances matter. A story about a particular looking glass should not be turned into a general rule that any reflective surface offers unrestricted travel.

Wonderland #17 adds a more specific piece of history. Calie and Violet investigate the location of the experiment associated with the first portal to Wonderland. The useful fact is the connection between a deliberate experiment and an opening between realms. The description does not supply a repeatable scientific procedure, establish that the experiment created Wonderland itself, or explain every later crossing.

A portal's origin, its operation, and a traveler's ability to use it are separate questions. Knowing where a crossing began does not make a character capable of opening one whenever necessary.

The realm can reach beyond its borders

Down the Rabbit Hole follows Alice after she has escaped Wonderland, with the realm's beings still threatening the people around her. The physical journey home therefore does not provide complete protection. A person can be back on Earth while the supernatural problem continues.

The distinction matters when discussing a magical cost. Some of what a survivor carries is the consequence of what happened. Some of the danger comes from an enemy that remains active. Calling both things a curse can blur the difference between an ongoing supernatural attack and the damage an earlier experience has already caused.

Wonderland's influence is often described through the language of madness or infection. In these stories, those are descriptions of a fictional supernatural horror. They should not be treated as a statement about real mental illness or a reason to assume that a frightened, distressed character is inherently dangerous.

The mind can become part of the conflict

Asylum provides one of the clearest early examples of a relationship between supernatural power and a person's mind. Its premise places the Jabberwocky within Alice's fractured mind, seeking release. This is more specific than saying the creature can simply do anything because Wonderland is strange.

The arrangement establishes both a danger and a restriction. There is something powerful trying to get free, and its freedom is not automatic. Alice's situation matters to that conflict. The human character is not merely observing a distant battle between monsters.

It would go too far to turn this into a general spell anyone can learn. The story establishes a particular imprisonment involving a particular being and person. It does not give every visitor the ability to trap a monster inside their own mind or guarantee that willpower alone can end such an imprisonment.

The Mad Hatter is more than a costume

Johnny's transformation is central to Through the Looking Glass, while the early ongoing series presents the Hatter threat through both a returning spirit and a dangerous hat. The official introduction to that ongoing series makes the object important by following a child who brings one home from a carnival.

Together, these stories make the Hatter identity something more complicated than a person deciding to dress like a familiar villain. The role has a history, and the associated danger can outlast a straightforward encounter with one individual.

The safe conclusion is that identities and objects can carry supernatural significance in Wonderland. A complete rule for how every Hatter succeeds another would require more than that. It is better to describe the particular transformation or manifestation than assume one automatic process governs every incarnation.

The Ebony Blade changes what is possible

The Ebony Blade is one of the clearest examples of a specific magical tool mattering. Wonderland #19 identifies it as the weapon associated with the end of the Jabberwocky's reign. Clash of Queens also calls it the Death Blade and makes its return a reason for the queens to compete.

Its importance comes from the possibility of achieving something that ordinary force cannot be assumed to achieve. A weapon with a special relationship to supernatural death changes the balance between beings who might otherwise feel secure. The holder gains leverage as well as a means of attack.

The blade's reputation also helps explain why possessing an object can become a political objective. Armies and powerful rulers still have reasons to pursue a single weapon. Strength, authority, and the right countermeasure are different kinds of advantage.

The early sources establish its exceptional role. They do not justify treating it as a universal answer to every supernatural problem in the wider Grimm Universe, regardless of the opponent or circumstances.

Power still has to contend with other power

The queens' struggle shows that Wonderland's rulers are not interchangeable with the realm itself. They have rivals, followers, weapons, and interests that can be frustrated. The Trickster's manipulation of their competition depends on those divisions.

That makes the political stories useful evidence about limits. If a ruler needs an army, seeks an artifact, or must maneuver around another faction, the story is not presenting that ruler as someone who can automatically erase all resistance.

Similarly, the aftermath leading into Call of Wonderland shows that overcoming a major threat does not settle every danger in the realm. A vacant position of power can create another crisis. The ability to defeat an enemy and the ability to make Wonderland permanently safe are not the same achievement.

Costs, limits, and what remains uncertain

The clearest costs in early Wonderland are consequences: physical harm, manipulation, loss of control, threatened family members, and an escape that fails to end the pursuit. These are substantial costs, but they are not presented as a numerical spellcasting system.

There is no reason to invent a fixed amount of energy consumed by a portal, a universal period before a power can be used again, or a rule that every magical act costs an equal portion of sanity. An individual bargain, object, or ability can have conditions without those conditions applying to the whole world.

For the same reason, surviving corruption once does not prove permanent immunity. A character's resistance in a particular confrontation is evidence about that confrontation. Future threats still need to be read on their own terms.

The practical picture is a world where access, identity, imprisonment, and possession of the right object can all determine the outcome. Wonderland's magic is frightening partly because those things can become entangled. A person may reach home without ending a pursuit, recognize an enemy without understanding its influence, or obtain a powerful weapon without gaining control of the conflict around it.

484. The Commission considers that the evidence is insufficient to determine whether or not these acts of genocide were planned or ordered by leaders at a higher level.

485. The Commission considers that, although it did not obtain, nor could it under the circumstances be expected to obtain, direct testimonial or documentary evidence to support it, circumstantial evidence is sufficient to warrant the conclusion that some highly placed members of FRODEBU had planned in advance a response to the very real eventuality of a coup by the Army, that such response included, together with blocking roads and arming Hutus, the taking of male Tutsi adults and youths as hostages, and that this plan had been made known in advance to certain local FRODEBU members in positions of leadership down to the level of the communes.

486. The Commission considers that the evidence shows that indiscriminate killing of Hutu men, women and children was carried out by members of the Burundian Army and Gendarmerie, and by Tutsi civilians. Although no evidence was obtained to indicate that the repression was centrally planned or ordered, it is an established fact that no effort was made by the military authorities at any level of command to prevent, stop, investigate or punish such acts. The Commission considers that this failure to act engages the responsibility of those military authorities with regard to such acts.

487. The Commission considers that, with the evidence at hand, it is not in a position to identify by name the persons that should be brought to justice for the acts to which these conclusions refer.

PART V: RECOMMENDATIONS

488. To make recommendations as to how to effect national reconciliation in Burundi and reestablish peace and security is, if not beyond the mandate, certainly beyond the means of the Commission. The Commission can hardly be expected to come up with miraculous solutions where the intensive, ongoing efforts by the United Nations and other members of the international community have so far shown no results in preventing, much less in redressing, the constant deterioration of the situation in Burundi.

489. The Commission, having gained a certain familiarity with conditions in the interior of the country, cannot fail to point out, however, that reported international efforts appear to concentrate on the redistribution of power among the political and military elite in Bujumbura, while little is heard of the basic problem of resettling the tens of thousands of internally displaced Tutsis and exiled Hutus, of restraining population growth, of creating opportunities for work outside of agriculture and of increasing agricultural yields, all of which would require considerable outside assistance.

I. IMPUNITY

490. Impunity has, without any doubt, been an important contributing factor in the aggravation of the ongoing crisis. But, while at the outset it was one of the causes of the present situation, it has now become an effect. To make the suppression of impunity a precondition for the solution of the crisis is completely unrealistic and can serve only to give excuses to those who are unwilling to take the necessary actions.

491. Impunity can only be suppressed through a fair and effective administration of justice. The Commission can find no way in which such an administration of justice can be established while the present situation of the country has not been brought under a minimum of control.

492. It is a fact that the Burundian judiciary and police are overwhelmingly unbalanced in favor of Tutsis, as is the entire legal profession. It is a fact that Burundian criminal law and criminal procedures need to be reformed. It is a fact that judges and prosecutors lack even the most essential material resources to accomplish their task. But all these facts pale before the central fact of overriding ethnic confrontation and total insecurity throughout the country. No amount of reforms or resources can have any effect as long as every citizen faces the ever present and very real danger of death at the hands of members of either ethnic group, and as long as every citizen is convinced that his own ethnic group is under attack by people who have repeatedly shown that they do not hesitate to commit mass murder. It is clearly impossible for any system of justice to function under such conditions.

493. The Commission believes that, whenever conditions in the country permit effective reforms to be made, the most important of these would be to establish a reasonable ethnic balance at all levels regarding judges, prosecutors and judiciary police. This would require that the appointment and removal of these functionaries be entrusted to an impartial, independent, non political and ethnically balanced body with the necessary power and public credibility. The judicial police, at present an almost non existent body, should be given the necessary manpower and resources and freed from ethnic or political control. It should be a purely civilian body, with no links to the Army or Gendarmerie. The present practice of indefinite detention without formal accusation or prosecution must be abolished.

494. It must be borne in mind that, among the present adult population of Burundi, tens, if not hundreds, of thousands of individuals from both ethnic groups have at one time or another committed homicide. To prosecute every one of them is clearly beyond any system of justice. If those who bear the main responsibility for these crimes are ever to be brought to justice, judges or prosecutors must be empowered to offer immunity or reduced sentences, in exchange for cooperation, to those who were merely ordered or led.

495. The establishment of an impartial and effective system of justice would require considerable international assistance in the form of training and financial support. A transitional period could be envisaged during which, to establish public credibility, foreign observers, recruited from the judiciary of other francophone African nations, would sit in the bi-ethnic courts and, if necessary, mediate between the judges.

II. GENOCIDE

496. Having concluded that acts of genocide against the Tutsi minority were committed in Burundi in October 1993, the Commission believes that international jurisdiction should be asserted with respect to these acts.

497. The Commission believes, however, that it is not possible to carry out an adequate international investigation of these acts while the present situation persists in Burundi.

498. If it is decided to assert international jurisdiction regarding acts of genocide in Burundi once a reasonable level of order and security and ethnic harmony are reestablished, the investigation should not be limited to acts committed in October 1993, but should also extend to other acts committed in the past, in order to determine whether they also constituted acts of genocide and, if such is found to be the case, to identify those responsible and bring them to justice. Particular attention should be given to the events that took place in 1972 when, according to all reports, a systematic effort was made to exterminate all educated Hutus. No one was ever prosecuted for these acts.

499. Any international body that is given the responsibility of investigating genocide in Burundi must be given sufficient resources and powers to inspect files and records, to command the disclosure of documents, to make witnesses appear before it, to ensure the punishment of perjury, to ensure the safety of witnesses and to guarantee immunity or reduced sentences to those willing to cooperate.

During the Second Wizarding War, Death Eaters kidnapped Luna and took her to Malfoy Manor, where she was held prisoner. Despite the danger, she never betrayed her friends or willingly gave Voldemort information that could put them at risk.

When Harry eventually finds Luna in the manor’s cellar, she has been through an experience no one should have to endure. Yet she still shows kindness and concern for others. Her circumstances had changed, but the qualities that defined her remained.

Luna had already fought alongside Dumbledore’s Army and later returned to fight in the Battle of Hogwarts. She never needed to be the strongest witch in the room or the centre of attention to prove her courage. She simply stood by the people she cared about, even when doing so put her life in danger.

Her friendship with Harry was built on that same quiet loyalty. Luna accepted him without judgment and offered him a kind of understanding that few others could. She became someone he valued, not because she sought his attention, but because of who she was.

📍 St. Augustine, Florida

On Anastasia Island, a striped lighthouse rises above the trees, its lantern looking out toward the Atlantic. Visitors come for the view. Others come wondering whether the tower has kept more than its maritime history.

In 1873, while the present lighthouse was under construction, a small railway cart carried supplies from the water to the building site. Children sometimes rode it for fun. On July 10, the cart overturned into the water. Mary and Eliza Pittee and another young girl, whose name has not been established in the museum's research, drowned. Four-year-old Carrie Pittee survived. A worker named Dan Sessions rushed to help and lifted the cart.

This tragedy is documented history, not a ghost legend. The lighthouse itself was completed in 1874, and its light first shone that October.

Some connect these experiences to the girls who died here. Those are witness accounts and folklore, not proof that spirits remain.

Imagine the wind coming off the water as you climb the spiral staircase. Each step echoes inside the tower. Somewhere below, a sound carries upward. Is it another visitor? The building settling? Or the sort of unexplained moment that keeps a legend alive for generations?

The lighthouse museum preserves the real history and offers after-dark tours for those curious enough to explore the stories themselves.

DID YOU KNOW?

Mike Ditka (then Saints HC) told the world he would trade his entire draft for Ricky Williams in the spring of 1999. He wasn’t bluffing.

The Saints had already given up their 2nd-round pick. Ditka still offered the rest of their 1999 picks plus future first- and third-rounders to move up and grab the Heisman-winning RB out of Texas.

When Indianapolis took Edgerrin James at No. 4, Washington took the package. Ditka got his guy at No. 5, put on a dreadlock wig, and celebrated as he’d just won the Super Bowl.

A couple of months later, ESPN The Magazine wanted Williams on the cover. Writer Dan Le Batard, who knew him from college, floated an idea: the massive trade was basically a marriage. What if they shot it that way?

Williams laughed and said yes. Ditka’s only condition: “I’m not wearing the dress.”

They rented a garden in Old Metairie. Williams put on a white wedding gown, veil, and tiara and held a bouquet. Ditka stood next to him in a tuxedo.

Photographer Greg Heisler caught the moment they looked at each other instead of the camera. The cover line read “For Better or Worse.” The subhead: “Ricky and Ditka take the plunge.”

The Saints’ PR people later said they felt misled and never would have approved it. Too late. The cover dropped in August 1999, and the reaction was immediate.

Plenty of people called it embarrassing. Williams has said that while he was putting on the dress, he had a brief “what did I get myself into?” moment, but he thought it was just a costume and a funny way to tell the story.
